items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in the http_download function of web-lib-funcs.pl that skips TLS chain and hostname verification. Man-in-the-middle attackers can present any certificate and substitute downloaded modules, themes, or catalog content, leading to root code execution or injected HTML.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Improper TLS Certificate Validation via http_download

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in apache/restart.cgi that displays the last five Apache ErrorLog lines without HTML escaping. Unauthenticated attackers can inject script into error_log via malformed requests or denied paths, executing in a Webmin user's session when Apache fails to restart.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via apache/restart.cgi Error Log Output

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in ldap-useradmin/raw.cgi that allows attackers with LDAP attribute write access to inject markup. Attackers can store script in user or group attributes or the dn, which executes in an administrator's browser when viewing the raw entry.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via ldap-useradmin/raw.cgi

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in generic_ldap_connect in ldap-client-lib.pl that accepts any LDAPS or StartTLS server certificate. Man-in-the-middle attackers can impersonate the LDAP server to capture the bind DN password, often the root DN, and return forged directory data.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Improper LDAP Certificate Validation in generic_ldap_connect

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a signature verification bypass vulnerability in webmin-lib.pl that allows attackers to install unsigned module updates when GnuPG setup fails. Attackers tampering with update downloads via network position or a custom update URL can supply malicious modules that run as root when administrators apply updates.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 GnuPG Signature Check Bypass in Module Updates

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in mailboxes/detach.cgi that allows unauthenticated mail senders to bypass the HTML sanitizer. Attackers can send HTML attachments with entity-obfuscated javascript: schemes or encoded script tags in iframe srcdoc to execute script in the Webmin session of users opening them.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via mailboxes/detach.cgi Attachment Viewer

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in mysql/view_table.cgi that allows MySQL users to inject scripts via unescaped column names. Attackers with CREATE or ALTER privilege can create columns containing HTML payloads that execute in a Webmin administrator's session when the table is viewed.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via mysql/view_table.cgi Column Names

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts by submitting malicious failed-login usernames. Attackers can repeatedly submit crafted usernames until blocked, executing script in administrator sessions viewing edit_blocked.cgi in Webmin or Usermin.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via Blocked Users Page

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Servers Index module that allows unauthenticated adjacent attackers to inject scripts via the realhost field of UDP discovery replies. Attackers on the same broadcast domain can answer discovery scans with HTML or JavaScript stored by find_servers() and rendered unescaped by edit_serv.cgi, executing in Webmin user sessions.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via Servers Index Discovery realhost Field

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows on-path network attackers to inject script by tampering with plaintext HTTP search results rendered unescaped. Attackers who intercept rpmfind.net or Google responses can inject autofocus/onfocus payloads that execute in a logged-in user's browser within the Webmin origin.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 XSS via software/rpmfind.cgi and man/search.cgi

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in lpadmin/list_jobs.cgi that allows local users or network IPP clients to inject script via CUPS print-job titles. Attackers can submit a print job with a crafted title, for example using lp -t, to execute script in a Printer Administration user's Webmin session.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via lpadmin/list_jobs.cgi Print Job Titles

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in ldap-server/edit_browser.cgi that allows attackers with write access to LDAP entry attributes to inject script by storing markup in attribute values. When an administrator browses the entry in the LDAP Server directory browser, the unencoded script runs in the Webmin origin, letting attackers act with the administrator's session.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via LDAP Server edit_browser.cgi

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains an insecure download vulnerability in webmin/upgrade.cgi, cluster-webmin/upgrade.cgi and cluster-usermin/upgrade.cgi that fetches upgrade packages over plaintext HTTP with GnuPG signature verification disabled by default. On-path network attackers can substitute a malicious RPM, Debian or tar.gz package during a default upgrade to execute code as root on the Webmin host and managed cluster servers.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Insecure Upgrade Download via Plaintext HTTP in upgrade.cgi

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject scripts by supplying values from managed hosts that cluster modules render unescaped. Attackers who can edit a Servers Index description, control a managed host, or intercept its RPC link can inject server descriptions, versions, user/group names, or package fields to execute JavaScript in the central administrator's session.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via Cluster Modules

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a Perl code injection vulnerability in cluster-useradmin/sync.cgi that allows attackers to run code by placing single quotes in home directory paths. Attackers with root on one managed host can craft a home path that breaks out of remote_eval() string literals during Sync, executing Perl as root on other managed hosts.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Perl Code Injection via cluster-useradmin/sync.cgi

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Upload and Download module that allows attackers to inject script via unescaped HTTP status lines from background downloads. Attackers controlling a download server can return a malicious status line stored by updown/download.pl and printed unescaped by updown/index.cgi, executing script in a higher-privileged user's session.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via Upload and Download Module

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in ldap-client/popup_browser.cgi that allows attackers to inject markup by storing it in LDAP attribute values printed without HTML encoding. Attackers with write access to an LDAP directory entry, needing no Webmin account, can execute scripts in the Webmin origin when an administrator browses that entry.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via LDAP Client popup_browser.cgi

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a cleartext transmission vulnerability in connect_ldap_db in ldap-server/ldap-server-lib.pl that sends the LDAP root DN password unencrypted when encryption is set to Detect automatically. Passive network attackers observing traffic between Webmin and a remote LDAP server can capture directory root credentials because the connection loop always reaches a plaintext bind attempt.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Cleartext LDAP Root DN Password Transmission via ldap-server-lib.pl

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in status/edit_mon.cgi that allows attackers to inject scripts through unescaped monitor status descriptions. Malicious HTTP or FTPS server operators, on-path attackers, or local users creating crafted filenames in wildcard-monitored directories can execute JavaScript in a Webmin user's session.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 XSS via status/edit_mon.cgi Monitor Descriptions

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a weak random password generation vulnerability in generate_random_password() that allows attackers to predict generated account passwords because seed_random() effectively seeds Perl rand() with only time XOR process ID. When the non-default random_password option is enabled and administrators keep the pre-filled password in edit_user.cgi, attackers can enumerate time and PID seeds to recover passwords and authenticate as new accounts.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Predictable Password Generation in Users and Groups Module

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in postfix/view_mailq.cgi and sendmail/view_mailq.cgi that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script via unsanitized MIME attachment filenames. Attackers can send a message with a crafted Content-Disposition or Content-Type filename that remains queued, executing script in the Webmin session of users viewing it.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via Mail Queue Attachment Filenames

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in mount/nfs_export.cgi that allows malicious NFS servers to inject scripts through unescaped export paths. Attackers controlling or spoofing an NFS server's mountd replies can return crafted export paths that execute JavaScript in the session of a Webmin user browsing exports.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 XSS via mount/nfs_export.cgi NFS Export Chooser

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in switch_smtp_to_ssl in mailboxes/boxes-lib.pl and status/smtp-monitor.pl, which calls Net::SSLeay::connect without certificate verification or a hostname check. Man-in-the-middle attackers can present any certificate when SMTP with SSL or STARTTLS is configured to capture SMTP AUTH credentials and message content.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Improper Certificate Validation in switch_smtp_to_ssl

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows local users or directory writers to inject script by placing markup in user names, group names or GECOS fields. Attackers can set GECOS via chfn or modify LDAP, NIS or SSSD entries so unescaped values in my_user_chooser.cgi, my_group_chooser.cgi, user_chooser.cgi and group_chooser.cgi execute in a Webmin user's browser.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via User and Group Chooser Popups

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Disk Quotas module that allows directory administrators to inject markup via NSS user names. Attackers who can create or rename LDAP, NIS or SSSD identities owning blocks on XFS quota filesystems can execute script in the browser of administrators viewing quota/list_users.cgi.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via quota/list_users.cgi

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in mysql/index.cgi that renders MySQL connection error text and server version strings without escaping. Malicious MySQL server operators or on-path attackers on plaintext connections can return markup in error packets or version strings to execute JavaScript in Webmin user sessions.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 XSS via MySQL Module mysql/index.cgi

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in the Perl Modules (cpan) module, which downloads CPAN indexes and module archives over plaintext HTTP without checksum or signature verification. On-path network attackers can answer the outbound fetch while an administrator installs a CPAN module, supplying a malicious Makefile.PL that cpan/download.cgi runs as root before confirmation.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 RCE via Plaintext CPAN Downloads in Perl Modules

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in ldap-useradmin/edit_user.cgi that allows attackers to inject markup through the LDAP sambaAcctFlags and sambaBadPasswordCount attributes, which are rendered without HTML encoding. Attackers with LDAP write access to these attributes can store malicious scripts that execute in a Webmin administrator's browser when the user entry is opened in the editor.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via LDAP Samba Attributes in edit_user.cgi

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability that allows man-in-the-middle attackers to capture credentials because servers/save_serv.cgi skips the selected SSL certificate check. When fast RPC is set to Automatic, attackers intercepting the /fastrpc.cgi probe can obtain the remote Webmin username and password sent via HTTP Basic Authorization.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Improper Certificate Validation in servers/save_serv.cgi Fast-RPC Probe

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in init/mass_systemd.cgi that prints unescaped journalctl output when a systemd service fails to start. Attackers can inject script into the journal via logger or sshd invalid user names, executing it in an administrator's Webmin session.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via init/mass_systemd.cgi Journal Output

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in servers/link.cgi that accepts self-signed certificates for linked servers even when certificate checking is enabled. Man-in-the-middle attackers presenting a self-signed certificate with the correct hostname can capture stored HTTP Basic credentials for the remote Webmin and inject HTML into the local Webmin origin.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Improper Certificate Validation via servers/link.cgi

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in ldap-client/check.cgi that allows LDAP directory writers to execute commands via unquoted uid values. Attackers can create a posixAccount entry with shell metacharacters in its uid, executing commands as root when an administrator runs Check Configuration.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 OS Command Injection via ldap-client/check.cgi

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a weak randomness vulnerability that allows attackers to predict TOTP two-factor secrets generated by generate_base32_secret() using a time and PID seeded rand(). Attackers who know a user's password and estimate enrollment time can enumerate candidate seeds, reproduce the secret, and bypass the second authentication factor.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Predictable TOTP Secret Generation via generate_base32_secret()

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a STARTTLS downgrade vulnerability in send_mail in mailboxes/boxes-lib.pl that continues over plaintext when STARTTLS is rejected. Man-in-the-middle attackers can strip or reject STARTTLS to capture configured SMTP AUTH credentials, crackable CRAM-MD5 exchanges, and the content of sent mail.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 STARTTLS Downgrade via send_mail in boxes-lib.pl

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a missing integrity verification vulnerability in usermin/upgrade.cgi that downloads Usermin upgrade packages over plaintext HTTP without signature or digest checks. On-path network attackers or DNS spoofers can supply a malicious RPM, Debian, or tar.gz package whose maintainer scripts or setup.sh execute as root during upgrade.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Insecure Usermin Upgrade Download via upgrade.cgi

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains an insecure default configuration in its Windows setup.bat script that provisions an administrator account with the credentials admin/admin and SSL disabled. Unauthenticated network attackers can log in over plain HTTP on port 10000 with these unchanged credentials to gain full Webmin administrative access.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Default Admin Credentials via Windows setup.bat

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in imap_login in mailboxes/folders-lib.pl that skips certificate verification and hostname checks for IMAP SSL connections. Man-in-the-middle attackers can present any certificate to capture IMAP credentials sent by the System and Server Status IMAP monitor and spoof monitor results.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Missing IMAP Certificate Validation in imap_login

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in minecraft/save_backup.cgi that allows local attackers with write access to the Minecraft server directory to inject script via unescaped world directory names. Attackers can create a world directory containing HTML or script that executes in a Webmin user's session when they run Backup Now.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via Minecraft save_backup.cgi

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in fastrpc.cgi that allows unauthenticated network peers to connect to tcpwrite and tcpread file-transfer listeners without session checks. Attackers can race to connect to the predictable transfer port during cluster operations to steal transferred files or replace staged packages, achieving root code execution.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Missing Authentication on fastrpc.cgi File-Transfer Sockets

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in password_change.cgi that allows unauthenticated attackers to change passwords for accounts with empty stored hashes. When passwd_mode is 2, attackers can POST user, old, new1 and new2 with any old value to set a known password and gain access.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Authentication Bypass via password_change.cgi

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a path traversal vulnerability in minecraft/minecraft-lib.pl that allows unauthenticated game players to overwrite arbitrary files as root via crafted chat messages. Attackers can send chat messages mimicking logged in lines so the root check_playtime_limits cron job rewrites attacker-chosen files, destroying their contents.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Path Traversal via Minecraft Server Playtime Limits

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in proc/trace.cgi that allows local unprivileged OS users to inject markup via unescaped process arguments and system call parameters. Attackers can craft process command lines or file names passed to open so that script executes in a Webmin user's session when they trace the process.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via proc/trace.cgi Running Processes Trace

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a cleartext transmission vulnerability in the SMTP service monitor that never issues STARTTLS because get_smtp_status tests an undefined $ssl variable. Passive network attackers can capture AUTH PLAIN credentials sent in plaintext each time a STARTTLS-configured monitor runs, without needing a Webmin login.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Cleartext Credential Transmission via status/smtp-monitor.pl

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a cleartext transmission vulnerability in web-lib-funcs.pl and fastrpc.cgi that sends cluster RPC traffic over raw TCP despite SSL configuration. Network-positioned attackers can read the session ID and remote_eval payloads or alter calls in transit to execute code as root on managed servers.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Cleartext Transmission of Fast RPC Traffic via fastrpc.cgi

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a header directive injection vulnerability in sendmail/autoreply.pl that allows unauthenticated mail senders to inject autoreply directives by placing them in inbound subject, from, date, or body fields. Attackers can inject Reply-Tracking to delete files at chosen paths, Autoreply-File to exfiltrate files readable by the delivery user, or arbitrary reply headers including To.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Header Directive Injection via sendmail/autoreply.pl

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in logrotate/force.cgi that prints logrotate -f diagnostic output without HTML escaping. Local OS users can create files with script-laden names in wildcard-rotated log directories, executing script in the Webmin session when Force Log Rotation is clicked.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via logrotate/force.cgi

items.summary: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in useradmin/edit_user.cgi that displays home directory paths without HTML escaping to users with the autohome ACL. A Webmin user with broader Users and Groups rights can store a home path containing script via save_user.cgi, executing it in a restricted sub-administrator's Webmin session.
items.title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via useradmin/edit_user.cgi Home Directory

items.summary: league/commonmark 2.6.0 before 2.10.8 contains a denial of service vulnerability in DelimiterStack::push() that miscounts delimiter runs against the max_delimiters_per_line budget. Attackers submitting Markdown with two long emphasis character runs can produce deeply nested strong elements, causing quadratic rendering time and CPU exhaustion.
items.title: league/commonmark 2.6.0 before 2.10.8 Denial of Service via max_delimiters_per_line Bypass

items.summary: COVESA Open1722 before 0.9.8 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in Avtp_Vss_CalcVssPathLength in src/avtp/acf/custom/Vss.c, which reads the INTEROP path-length prefix without checking the declared ACF message length. Attackers can send header-only 12-byte INTEROP-mode VSS frames to trigger reads past the buffer, or prefix values 0xFFFE and 0xFFFF that wrap uint16 lengths and cause Avtp_Vss_SetVssData to overwrite the path area.
items.title: COVESA Open1722 before 0.9.8 Out-of-Bounds Read via Avtp_Vss_CalcVssPathLength

items.summary: Shopify async-memcached before 0.11.0 contains a command injection vulnerability in Client::validate_meta_flags that allows attackers to inject extra memcached meta protocol tokens via whitespace in flags. Attackers controlling part of a meta flag can add quiet, opaque, mode or size override tokens to alter operations and desynchronize responses on shared connections.
items.title: Shopify async-memcached before 0.11.0 Meta Protocol Injection via Meta Flags

items.summary: Karakeep before 0.35.0 contains an improper access control vulnerability in ManualList.mergeInto that allows list owners to retain collaborator bookmarks by merging shared lists without ownership checks. Owners invoking the lists.merge tRPC procedure create rows not tied to collaborator membership, preserving read access to collaborator bookmarks and assets after the collaborator's access is revoked.
items.title: Karakeep before 0.35.0 Improper Access Control via lists.merge Procedure

items.summary: Karakeep before 0.35.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows shared-list collaborators to learn other users' private favourited and archived bookmark state through filter queries. Viewer or editor collaborators can call bookmarks.getBookmarks on a shared list with favourited or archived set to true, inferring owners' private flags from which bookmarks buildCommonFilters returns.
items.title: Karakeep before 0.35.0 Information Disclosure via Shared-List Bookmark Filters

items.summary: pain001-mcp 0.0.72 before 0.0.80 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the commit_payment_batch MCP tool that allows attackers to write files outside any output directory via output_file_path. Attackers can stage a batch, reuse the self-issued confirmation_token, and supply absolute, dot-dot, or symlinked paths to create or overwrite server-writable files with generated XML.
items.title: pain001-mcp 0.0.72 before 0.0.80 Arbitrary File Write via commit_payment_batch

items.summary: LTplus-AG ifc-lite @ifc-lite/export before 4.13.1 and ifc-lite-export before 27.0.0 contain a STEP record injection vulnerability in the mutation writer via unescaped typed-value type names. Attackers controlling the mutations payload can place parentheses, semicolons, and newlines in typed.type to append arbitrary entity records to exported IFC files, bypassing the class-name guard.
items.title: LTplus-AG ifc-lite @ifc-lite/export before 4.13.1 and ifc-lite-export before 27.0.0 STEP Record Injection

items.summary: WeKan before 12.78 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in Exporter.buildStream() that lets attackers retrieve checklists from other boards by supplying a checklistId export scope. Users able to export any board, or unauthenticated users via a public board, can read private checklists, their items and creator usernames even when anonymization is enabled.
items.title: WeKan before 12.78 Information Disclosure via Board Export checklistId Parameter

items.summary: WeKan before 12.78 contains an access control bypass in Exporter.buildCsvStream() that ignores the Disable all export and Anonymize export users settings. Board readers or unauthenticated users of public boards can request the CSV export endpoint to export all cards and reveal real usernames in member, assignee, and mention fields.
items.title: WeKan before 12.78 Export Restriction Bypass via Streaming CSV/TSV Export

items.summary: lightNVR before 0.44.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in go2rtc_proxy_authorize_request() that allows authenticated users to access restricted cameras by exploiting inconsistent src parameter parsing. Attackers can percent-encode a second src parameter name or exceed the 255-byte truncation so go2rtc resolves a different camera, obtaining unauthorized snapshots and HLS live streams.
items.title: lightNVR before 0.44.3 Authorization Bypass via go2rtc Proxy src Parameter

items.summary: ai-memory 2.6.0 before 3.3.2 contains a symlink following vulnerability in the ai-memory-wikisync companion that allows local attackers to overwrite arbitrary files by planting symlinks at predictable temporary names. Attackers can place a .wikisync-tmp-<page>.md symlink in a shared destination so atomic_write() truncates and overwrites its target with the victim's privileges.
items.title: ai-memory 2.6.0 before 3.3.2 Symlink Arbitrary File Overwrite via ai-memory-wikisync

items.summary: SRS 4.0.0 before 6.0.194, 7.0.0 before 7.0.214, and 8.0.0 before 8.0.73 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in SrsRtcpCommon::decode and SrsRtcpTWCC::decode that lets remote WebRTC peers write past the fixed 1500-byte payload_ array. Unauthenticated attackers opening a WHIP or WHEP session can send oversized BYE, APP, unknown-type or TWCC RTCP packets to overwrite up to 64 KB of heap memory, crashing the server.
items.title: SRS before 6.0.194, 7.0.214, and 8.0.73 Heap Buffer Overflow via RTCP Decoding

items.summary: SRS 4.0.0 before 6.0.194, 7.0.0 before 7.0.214, and 8.0.0 before 8.0.73 contains a reachable assertion in RTCP decoding that lets remote WebRTC peers crash the server. Attackers opening an unauthenticated WHIP or WHEP session can send an 8-byte RTCP packet with undersized length, triggering srs_assert aborts that stop every stream.
items.title: SRS before 6.0.194, 7.0.214, and 8.0.73 Reachable Assertion via RTCP Length

items.summary: Wails before 2.17.1 on Linux contains an origin validation error in the sendMessageToBackend WebKitGTK handler that allows child-frame scripts to invoke the privileged IPC channel. Attackers controlling content loaded in an iframe can post messages that pass the top-level URI origin check and call bound Go methods and Wails runtime operations.
items.title: Wails before 2.17.1 on Linux Origin Validation Error via IPC Bridge

items.summary: Nektos act 0.2.92 before 0.2.95 contains an argument injection vulnerability in readProjectArgsFile and projectFlag that allows malicious repositories to bypass the untrusted project .actrc flag allowlist. Attackers can commit a crafted .actrc smuggling disallowed flags like -P self-hosted or --privileged to run workflow steps on the developer's host.
items.title: Nektos act 0.2.92 before 0.2.95 .actrc Allowlist Bypass via Argument Smuggling

items.summary: Electerm before 5.9.0 contains an origin validation vulnerability in the MCP Server widget that allows remote attackers to execute commands by bypassing Host and Origin checks through DNS rebinding. Attackers can lure users to a page that rebinds to 127.0.0.1 and calls unauthenticated MCP tools on port 30837 to run OS commands locally and on open SSH sessions.
items.title: Electerm before 5.9.0 RCE via DNS Rebinding in MCP Server Widget

items.summary: Mastodon 4.7.4 and 4.8.0-alpha.3 before 5.0.0-beta.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in authenticate_with_sign_in_token that allows authenticated local users to rebind pending login attempts to other accounts. Attackers can submit sign_in_token_resend with a victim's user[email] parameter, then guess the unthrottled 6-character token to sign in as inactive accounts lacking two-factor authentication.
items.title: Mastodon 4.7.4 and 4.8.0-alpha.3 before 5.0.0-beta.1 Authentication Bypass via Sign-In Token

items.summary: OpenProject 17.2.0 before 17.5.2, 17.6.0 before 17.6.1, 17.7.0 before 17.7.3, 17.8.0 before 17.8.2, and 17.9.0 before 17.9.7 contains an externally controlled method selection vulnerability in InplaceEditFieldsController via the unvalidated attribute parameter. Users who can view a project can request the inplace_edit_fields reset route with attribute destroy to delete projects and subprojects, or invoke other methods exposing restricted data.
items.title: OpenProject 17.2.0 before 17.5.2, 17.6.1, 17.7.3, 17.8.2, 17.9.7 Arbitrary Method Invocation

items.summary: A vulnerability was found in browser-use 0.13.13/0.13.14. This impacts the function load_and_migrate_config of the file browser_use/config.py of the component SecurityWatchdog. The manipulation results in improper authorization. The attack requires a local approach. The exploit has been made public and could be used.
items.title: browser-use SecurityWatchdog config.py load_and_migrate_config improper authorization

items.summary: A vulnerability has been found in JaguarJack catch-admin up to 5.4.1. This affects the function update of the file modules/Permissions/Http/Controllers/RolesController.php. The manipulation leads to dynamically-determined object attributes. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The identifier of the patch is 3ae60d57ea6840bb33456596ad799b0a39ca94a2. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.
items.title: JaguarJack catch-admin RolesController.php update dynamically-determined object attributes

items.summary: A flaw has been found in JaguarJack catch-admin up to 5.4.1. The impacted element is the function store of the file modules/Permissions/Http/Controllers/RolesController.php. Executing a manipulation can lead to dynamically-determined object attributes. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. This patch is called 3ae60d57ea6840bb33456596ad799b0a39ca94a2. It is best practice to apply a patch to resolve this issue.
items.title: JaguarJack catch-admin RolesController.php store dynamically-determined object attributes

items.summary: Akaunting 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the XLSX tax-import workflow. An authenticated Manager can import HTML in a tax name and associate the tax with an item. When an Administrator attempts to disable that tax, Akaunting renders the original stored name in an error notification through Vue v-html, causing attacker-controlled markup to execute within the browser of another authenticated user.
items.title: Akaunting 3.3.0 - Stored cross-site scripting through imported tax names in update notifications

items.summary: A vulnerability was detected in JaguarJack catch-admin up to 5.4.1. The affected element is the function Store/Update of the file modules/User/Http/Controllers/UserController.php of the component User Management. Performing a manipulation results in dynamically-determined object attributes. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. items.summary:
The vendored zcbor decoder's zcbor_any_skip() in boot/zcbor/src/zcbor_decode.c descends one C-stack frame per level of CBOR nesting. On a list or map it copies the decoder state (memcpy(&state_copy, state, sizeof(zcbor_state_t))) and recurses once per member, with no depth cap: the skip path does not use zcbor's backup stack, and ZCBOR_MAX_ELEM_COUNT is SIZE_MAX, so nothing bounds how deep the recursion goes.

That function is reached on attacker-controlled bytes before any authentication. MCUboot's serial-recovery command parser decodes SMP/CBOR requests with zcbor_map_decode_bulk() (boot/boot_serial/src/zcbor_bulk.c), which skips any map key it does not recognise by calling zcbor_any_skip() on the encoded value; the echo handler in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c calls it directly on the same footing. Both run during image upload, long before the uploaded image's signature is checked. The default receive buffer is MCUBOOT_SERIAL_MAX_RECEIVE_SIZE = 512 bytes and each nesting level costs a single byte to encode (0x81), so roughly 500 levels of nesting fit in one request — comfortably more than a bootloader's stack can absorb, since every frame carries a full zcbor_state_t copy plus locals.

The impact is availability only: the bootloader's stack overflows and the device faults or hangs during recovery. There is no controlled out-of-bounds write that escapes the DFU buffer, no disclosure, and no authentication bypass — the recursion grows the stack with the decoder's own internal state. Whether a given board actually exhausts its stack depends on that board's bootloader stack size, which we did not measure; the fix is nevertheless unconditional, because an unauthenticated pre-authentication code path must not have its safety depend on a per-board stack margin.

Exposure requires MCUBOOT_SERIAL (serial/SMP recovery), which is not enabled by default, and recovery entry is normally gated on a physical pin (CONFIG_BOOT_SERIAL_ENTRANCE_GPIO / PIN_RESET), with a no-valid-image fallback path. Products that expose serial recovery over an externally reachable transport, or that fall into recovery when no valid image is present, are the ones at risk.

The fix is to bound the skip: thread a recursion-depth counter through zcbor_any_skip() (or have zcbor_map_decode_bulk() reject values nested beyond a small constant) and fail once the limit is exceeded — equivalently, take the bounded-skip implementation from upstream zcbor.
items.title: Unbounded CBOR recursion in MCUboot serial recovery allows pre-authentication stack exhaustion

items.summary:
Summary

MCUboot enforces several security-critical invariants on the boot, image-swap, and validation paths using assert(). In a standard release/production build (NDEBUG defined) assert() expands to a no-op, so an invariant the code intends to halt on instead falls through, and execution continues with the bad or inconsistent state. Where the guarded condition is attacker-influenceable through the flash-write boundary (serial-recovery / DFU), this is a security check that is simply absent in release builds.

This is one root cause (assert-as-security-guard, no-op under NDEBUG) with one fix approach (replace the security-critical asserts with real fail-closed checks), so it is filed as a single advisory covering the enumerated sites.

Worst reachable instance — inconsistent swap status completes the swap without validation

In the swap-resume status read, an inconsistent status (erased_sections > 1) is detected, logged, and — when MCUBOOT_VALIDATE_PRIMARY_SLOT is disabled — is meant to abort, because "there is no way to be sure the swapped primary slot is OK." The abort is assert(0):

boot/bootutil/src/swap_move.c:181-194 — if (erased_sections > 1) { ... #if !defined(MCUBOOT_VALIDATE_PRIMARY_SLOT) / ... abort! / assert(0); #endif }, then execution falls through to compute bs->op/idx/state from the inconsistent status (lines 197-208) and return 0 (success).
boot/bootutil/src/swap_offset.c:266-280 — identical pattern; falls through to bs->op/idx/state and return 0.
boot/bootutil/src/swap_scratch.c:227-241 — same invalid/assert(0) pattern for the scratch backend.

Under NDEBUG with primary-slot validation off, the inconsistent status is neither aborted (assert is a no-op) nor re-validated (validation off), so boot_complete_partial_swap() finishes the swap on inconsistent metadata and the primary slot is booted without a signature check. An attacker who can write the swap-status trailer can craft the inconsistent status.

Reachability (threat model). Secondary slot + scratch trailers are A2-writable by definition (that is what a DFU upload is). Under MCUBOOT_SERIAL_RECOVERY the primary trailer is A2-writable too: boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c:978 opens flash_area_id_from_multi_image_slot(img_num, 0) (== primary) and writes from offset 0 bounded by area_size, so it can paint the primary swap-status/magic. This is how the A2 (recovery/DFU, unauthenticated by design) attacker influences the guarded condition. Property violated: P1 (image authenticity / secure-boot bypass) when un-revalidated content is booted, and P6 (boot/recovery availability).

Second reachable instance — resume-path swap_size from an unguarded trailer

boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:1190-1193: the swap resume branch does fap = boot_find_status(...); assert(fap != NULL); rc = boot_read_swap_size(fap, &bs->swap_size); assert(rc == 0);. boot_find_status() (boot/bootutil/src/bootutil_misc.c:166-204) searches {scratch, primary} and, on no-valid-magic-match, returns the last-iterated area (primary), not NULL — so assert(fap != NULL) cannot fire even in debug, and under NDEBUG neither assert fires. swap_size is then read from an A2-writable (serial-recovery primary, or scratch) trailer with no fail-closed handling. This is the same swap-metadata-trust family as the recorded resume/swap_size disclosure.

Reachable-security sites (center the fix here)

1. boot/bootutil/src/swap_move.c:193 — inconsistent-status assert(0), falls through to complete swap. A2 + !VALIDATE_PRIMARY. [worst]
2. boot/bootutil/src/swap_offset.c:278 — same, swap-offset backend.
3. boot/bootutil/src/swap_scratch.c:239 — same, swap-scratch backend.
4. boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:1191 and :1193 — resume assert(fap != NULL) / assert(rc == 0) guarding swap_size read from an A2-writable trailer; compounded by boot_find_status() never returning NULL.

(Truncated. The full description is in the advisory: https://github.com/mcu-tools/mcuboot/security/advisories/GHSA-cr9j-p626-pwcc)

items.summary:
MCUboot's encrypted serial-recovery path contains an attacker-controlled out-of-bounds stack write in decrypt_region_inplace() in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c. The routine decrypts an uploaded encrypted image one flash sector at a time into a sector-sized stack VLA buf[sz], but when the current sector is still inside the image header it sets the destination index to the absolute header size (idx = hdr->ih_hdr_size; at boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c:156) and then decrypts into &buf[idx]. The correct sibling routine boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:876 uses the sector-relative idx = hdr->ih_hdr_size - abs_off; the serial path is missing the - abs_off term, so for any sector after the first the index runs past the end of the stack buffer.

The ih_hdr_size field is a uint16_t taken verbatim from the uploaded image header. On the second sector onward, when ih_hdr_size exceeds the sector size, &buf[idx] points beyond buf and boot_enc_decrypt() writes attacker-controlled plaintext into adjacent stack frames. The path is reached pre-authentication: bs_upload() calls boot_handle_enc_fw() (boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c:1208) after upload, and the pre-decryption signature gate in decrypt_image_inplace() is compiled out (#if 0 at boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c:226-233), so the header is never validated before decryption.

A second error in the same window computation affects the first sector. When a sector holds both the end of the header and the start of the TLV area, the decrypt length is clamped to tlv_off - (off + bytes_copied), measured from the start of the sector rather than from idx (boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c:166). An encrypted image whose header and payload end within the first sector is therefore decrypted for ih_hdr_size bytes more than it should be: into the TLV area and, when the image ends near the end of the sector, past buf. This form needs no oversized header, so even an ordinary small encrypted image can trigger it, and it reaches devices with sectors of up to about 128 KiB rather than only those whose sector is smaller than the 16-bit ih_hdr_size.

Reaching the sink requires a build with MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES and serial recovery enabled, and access to the device's serial/USB recovery interface (unauthenticated by design). With the public-key encryption schemes the AES content key is wrapped to the device's public encryption key, so an attacker can author a fully crafted encrypted image — including a malicious ih_hdr_size — without the image-signing private key. The result is a controllable stack memory-corruption inside the bootloader before any signature check, providing a path to code execution in the secure-boot root of trust that bypasses image authentication, as well as a denial-of-service. A 2048-byte out-of-bounds write was reproduced under AddressSanitizer (sz=4096, off=4096, ih_hdr_size=6144).

On releases before v2.0.0 (v1.9.0 and v1.10.0) the destination is a file-scope static uint8_t buf[SOC_FLASH_ERASE_BLK_SZ] in .bss rather than the stack VLA described above — the code then lived in boot/zephyr/single_loader.c, before commit c9fa6088 relocated it to boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c and changed the buffer's storage class. The out-of-bounds write is equally real and equally pre-authentication on those releases, but it corrupts adjacent static data rather than the stack, so a stack-smashing proof of concept written against a current release will not reproduce as-is there.
items.title: Pre-authentication out-of-bounds write in MCUboot encrypted serial recovery image decryption
