Prior to 4.5.12 and 4.6.02, an attacker who can reach an image-upload flow can upload a valid image with appended PHP short-tag code and a double-extension filename. NukeViet\Files\Upload::save_file() relied on verify_image(), which missed the <? short-open tag, while filename handling preserved embedded dots, validation inspected only the final extension, and an .htaccess rule blocked PHP extensions only at the end of the URI. On Apache mod_php systems configured with short_open_tag and a PHP extension handler, the stored polyglot can execute as PHP and run operating-system commands as the web-server user; PHP-FPM, nginx, and end-anchored handler configurations are not exposed to the execution step. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.12 and 4.6.02.
items.title: NukeViet CMS: Remote Code Execution via image-upload bypass chain (PHP short-tag detection bypass + double-extension filename)

items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. In 4.6.00, an unauthenticated attacker can place the configured domain in X-Forwarded-Host while choosing a different destination in the ordinary Host header. The earlier fix validates only the forwarded value in includes/mainfile.php, while set_ini_file() in includes/ini.php constructs an outbound cURL request from the separately retained NV_SERVER_NAME before the ordinary host is rejected. Redirect following can carry the blind request to an attacker-selected private host, port, and path and invoke internal HTTP endpoints. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.
items.title: NukeViet: Pre-authentication SSRF via incomplete X-Forwarded-Host fix

items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.09, a user with news-posting permission can bypass NukeViet\Core\Request::filterAttr() by prefixing an event-handler attribute with an ASCII form-feed character, which PHP trimming preserves but browsers treat as whitespace. NukeViet\Core\Request::unhtmlentities() omitted a decimal HTML entity tab embedded in a javascript: URI. These parser differences allow persistent event handlers or script URLs to survive filtering in vendor/vinades/nukeviet/Core/Request.php and execute for visitors, including administrators. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.
items.title: NukeViet CMS: Multiple Anti-XSS Filter Bypasses Leading to Stored XSS in News Module

items.summary: mcp-ssh-manager is an MCP server for managing servers over SSH with human approval, an encrypted vault, and a live audit trail. Prior to 3.8.5, ssh_backup_create, ssh_backup_restore, ssh_backup_schedule, and ssh_backup_list build remote shell commands from caller-controlled values in src/backup-manager.js and inline backup handlers in src/index.js without neutralizing shell metacharacters. Crafted database, connection, backup directory, path, exclusion, schedule, or comment arguments can therefore execute arbitrary OS commands on managed remote servers as the configured SSH user. ssh_backup_schedule can persist execution through cron. ssh_backup_list does not pass through the server policy check and remains available in readonly and restricted modes, allowing command execution despite those restrictions. Tool arguments can be supplied by a malicious or compromised MCP client or steered through indirect prompt injection; fully trusted benign arguments do not trigger the issue. The earlier database-helper remediation for CVE-2026-77383 applied shell quoting to src/database-manager.js but did not cover these parallel backup builders. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.5.
items.title: mcp-ssh-manager: Remote code execution (RCE) via command injection in the backup subsystem

items.summary: mcp-ssh-manager is an MCP server for managing servers over SSH with human approval, an encrypted vault, and a live audit trail. Prior to 3.6.7, ssh_db_list, ssh_db_dump, ssh_db_import, and ssh_db_restore in src/database-manager.js interpolate caller-controlled database, table, collection, file path, user, host, port, and password values into shell-evaluated command strings without neutralization. Shell metacharacters in these arguments therefore execute arbitrary commands on the configured SSH target as the account used by the MCP server. ssh_db_list is classified as read-only and remains available in readonly and restricted server security modes, so this path bypasses the command-execution boundary those modes are intended to enforce. The dump and import builders are blocked in readonly mode but remain vulnerable in the default unrestricted mode. The earlier version 3.6.5 hardening covered only ssh_db_query query text; it did not protect the list, dump, import, or restore builders, or the connection flags used by query builders. This issue is fixed in version 3.6.7.
items.title: mcp-ssh-manager: Command injection in mcp-ssh-manager database helpers (ssh_db_list / ssh_db_dump / ssh_db_import)

items.summary: pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. Prior to 3.69.1, core/hooks/block-credential-reads.sh, core/hooks/block-egress.sh, core/hooks/block-fs-boundary.sh, and core/hooks/block-mcp-writes.sh pin PATH to /usr/bin:/bin, hard-code jq as /usr/bin/jq, and return success when jq is unavailable there. On systems where jq exists only in a Homebrew path, including affected pre-Sequoia or Homebrew-only macOS installations, the hooks can skip credential-read, network-egress, filesystem-boundary, and MCP-write controls. Native deny rules independently protect some credential paths but do not backstop the egress or MCP controls. An attacker who can influence a prompt, repository, or evaluation flow can use the skipped checks to expose secrets or perform unauthorized tool actions. This issue is fixed in version 3.69.1.
items.title: pmo-platform: Security Hooks Fail Open Because Runtime PATH Excludes Documented jq Install Paths

items.summary: LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.6.0, the authenticated GET /lists/{list}/feed and GET /tags/{tag}/feed handlers in app/Http/Controllers/App/FeedController.php use integer route model binding without an object-level authorization or visibility check. Unlike the web list controller, which invokes LinkListPolicy::view(), the feed controller lets a normal authenticated user enumerate another user's private list or tag and receive its name and feed metadata, along with public or internal bookmark entries associated with that taxonomy. The existing per-link visibility filter still excludes PRIVATE link records, so the disclosure is limited to the private taxonomy and its non-private member links. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.
items.title: LinkAce: IDOR on Authenticated Atom Feed Endpoints Exposes Private List and Tag Names Without Authorization Check

items.summary: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 3.1.0 until 4.5.1, the afpd Spotlight RPC fetchQueryResultsForContext: reply path in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c calls the top-level sl_pack function from sl_pack_filemeta on a shifted sub-buffer without passing the remaining capacity of the outer DSI reply buffer. An authenticated AFP client can request an amplified nested file-metadata tree so the nested packer applies MAX_SLQ_DAT relative to the shifted pointer and writes beyond struct DSI::data. The out-of-bounds write corrupts heap memory beyond the DSI reply buffer. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.1.
items.title: Netatalk: afpd Spotlight RPC heap-buffer-overflow in nested sl_pack_filemeta() marshalling

items.summary: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 3.1.0 until 4.5.0, sl_unpack_loop in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c uses an attacker-controlled Spotlight table-of-contents index during FPSpotlightRPC without checking it against the number of entries or the remaining dsi->commands buffer. An authenticated AFP client with access to a Spotlight-enabled volume can choose a large toc_index whose multiplication and addition produce an out-of-range address, causing an attacker-influenced heap read and reliably crashing the worker serving that session. The earlier CVE-2026-44066 remediation bounded recursion depth and toc_offset but did not bound toc_index. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.0.
items.title: Netatalk: Heap out-of-bounds read in afpd Spotlight RPC unmarshalling via unbounded toc_index in sl_unpack_loop()

items.summary: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 3.1.0 until 4.5.0, the afpd FPSpotlightRPC unmarshalling handlers in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c trust the element count encoded in the upper 32 bits of an RPC tag without comparing it with the remaining input length. An authenticated client with access to a Spotlight-enabled volume can make sl_unpack_ints, sl_unpack_date, sl_unpack_uuid, or sl_unpack_floats iterate beyond dsi->commands and read heap memory. The read values remain in internal dalloc storage and no information-disclosure channel was demonstrated, but the worker serving the attacker's session can be crashed. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.0.
items.title: Netatalk: Heap out-of-bounds read in afpd Spotlight RPC unmarshalling via unbounded element count in sl_unpack_ints() and sibling handlers

items.summary: Inscriptis is a Python library for converting HTML to text. From 2.0.0 until 2.7.6, when the parent is block-level, table_end_handler() in model/tag/table_tag.py writes each sibling table through HtmlElement.write_verbatim_text() in model/html_element.py; Canvas.open_block() leaves the parent padding_inline prefix on the stack, Canvas.close_block() does not remove it, and only Canvas.close_tag() calls prefix.remove_last_prefix(). Each following sibling table therefore carries forward accumulated indentation, making get_text() output grow quadratically and allowing small attacker-controlled HTML to exhaust memory in applications converting it without authentication or user interaction. This issue is fixed in 2.7.6.
items.title: Inscriptis: Quadratic memory growth from sibling <table> elements in get_text()

items.summary: memtomem-stm is a short-term memory proxy gateway with proactive memory surfacing for AI agents. From 0.1.0 until 0.1.34, untrusted long-term and working-memory fields can introduce Markdown or HTML-compatible structure into the surfaced-memory envelope because those fields are not serialized as inert data. A crafted memory can create misleading structural boundaries or visually conceal surfaced content, affecting how a consuming agent interprets the memory context. Ordinary natural-language persuasion remains a residual model-level risk and is outside the structural serialization flaw. This issue is fixed in version 0.1.34.
items.title: memtomem-stm: Surfaced memory data can escape the Markdown compatibility boundary

items.summary: one-hub through 0.14.27 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in GetImageFromUrl in common/image/image.go that fetches vision chat image_url values without destination restrictions. Attackers holding a standard non-admin API token can send crafted /v1/chat/completions requests via Claude, OpenRouter or Ollama providers to reach internal services or cloud metadata endpoints.
items.title: one-hub through 0.14.27 SSRF via Vision Chat image_url

items.summary: A vulnerability was found in sonos tract up to 0.23.4. The affected element is the function InferenceRulesOp::rules of the file onnx/src/ops/math/gemm.rs of the component Operand Arity Indexing. The manipulation of the argument inputs/outputs results in out-of-bounds read. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. Upgrading to version 0.23.5 is sufficient to fix this issue. The patch is identified as 44c6f4a7ef988a5bafe98c8bb465d8a253599395. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.
items.title: sonos tract Operand Arity Indexing gemm.rs rules out-of-bounds

items.summary: Mongoose Embedded Web Server / Networking Library before 7.24 contains a WebSocket fragmentation validation vulnerability that allows remote attackers to spoof message metadata by sending a single CONTINUATION frame with FIN=1 as the first data frame instead of a required TEXT/BINARY start frame, violating RFC 6455 sequencing rules. Attackers can craft this malformed frame to make mg_ws_cb() in src/ws.c misinterpret the first byte of payload as saved FIN/opcode flags, causing the application to receive a dispatched MG_EV_WS_MSG event with attacker-controlled flags and data truncated by one byte without closing the connection.
items.title: Mongoose before 7.24 WebSocket Frame Validation Bypass via ws.c

items.summary: A vulnerability was identified in OpenZipkin Zipkin 3.6.1. This affects the function UnzippingBytesRequestConverter.convertRequest of the file zipkin-server/src/main/java/zipkin2/server/internal/ZipkinHttpCollector.java of the component HTTP Collector. Such manipulation leads to highly compressed data. The attack can be executed remotely. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.
items.title: OpenZipkin HTTP Collector ZipkinHttpCollector.java UnzippingBytesRequestConverter.convertRequest data amplification

items.summary: free5GC PCF through 1.4.6 contains a resource leak in postAppSessCtxProcedure that leaves PCC rules and QoS data in the SM policy decision after rejected Npcf_PolicyAuthorization create requests. Authenticated AFs knowing an active PDU session's UE address can send repeated failing requests with distinct AF application identifiers to grow PCF memory and pollute policy sent to the SMF.
items.title: free5GC PCF through 1.4.6 Orphaned PCC Rules via Rejected Application Session Creation

items.summary: diffpy.structure before 3.5.1 contains a code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run Python code by supplying crafted CIF symmetry operations passed to eval() in get_symop(). Attackers can embed expressions in the _space_group_symop_operation_xyz or _symmetry_equiv_pos_as_xyz loop to execute code with victim privileges when the CIF file is parsed locally.
items.title: diffpy.structure before 3.5.1 Code Execution via eval in get_symop CIF Parsing

items.summary: A vulnerability was identified in Gladys Assistant up to 4.71.0. This affects an unknown function of the file gateway.downloadBackup.js of the component Backup Restore Endpoint. The manipulation of the argument file_url leads to os command injection. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. Upgrading to version 4.72.0 mitigates this issue. Upgrading the affected component is recommended.
items.title: Gladys Assistant Backup Restore Endpoint gateway.downloadBackup.js os command injection

items.summary: A flaw has been found in Konstanty libmodplug up to 0.8.9.1. The affected element is the function abc_add_drum of the file src/load_abc.cpp of the component ABC File Handler. Executing a manipulation can lead to out-of-bounds read. The attack may be performed from remote. Upgrading to version 0.8.9.2 is sufficient to fix this issue. This patch is called 540f0b8ec3d7979e17a8d6a55e31b8a7b734d463. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.
items.title: Konstanty libmodplug ABC File load_abc.cpp abc_add_drum out-of-bounds

items.summary: A security flaw has been discovered in nodejs undici up to 7.24.0. This affects the function Object.assign of the file balanced-pool.js of the component BalancedPool. The manipulation results in improperly controlled modification of object prototype attributes. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. Upgrading to version 7.24.1 is able to mitigate this issue. The patch is identified as 0d7ec33ff37563d3e7c98d11d7bca736f330d156. You should upgrade the affected component.
items.title: nodejs undici BalancedPool balanced-pool.js Object.assign prototype pollution

items.summary: A flaw has been found in hrshadhin CloudSchool up to 3.0.1. Affected by this issue is the function PublicController.checkSanity4Student of the file app/Http/Controllers/Backend/PublicController.php of the component Student Data Access Check. This manipulation of the argument student_id causes authorization bypass. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.
items.title: hrshadhin CloudSchool Student Data Access Check PublicController.php PublicController.checkSanity4Student authorization

items.summary: lwext4 through 1.0.0 contains a heap buffer overflow in ext4_fs_init_inode_bitmap() in src/ext4_fs.c because it does not validate s_inodes_per_group against the inode bitmap size. Attackers can supply a crafted ext4 image with an oversized s_inodes_per_group so memset writes past the heap buffer, corrupting memory and crashing the mounting application.
items.title: lwext4 through 1.0.0 Heap Buffer Overflow via ext4_fs_init_inode_bitmap

items.summary: A vulnerability was identified in Dolibarr ERP CRM up to 23.0.4. This affects the function dol_convert_file in the library htdocs/core/lib/files.lib.php of the component Document Upload. Such manipulation leads to code injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. Upgrading to version 24.0.0 is able to mitigate this issue. The name of the patch is 9b6368b2a9eae3eec690b2ce22c4f291f0051540. Upgrading the affected component is advised.
items.title: Dolibarr ERP CRM Document Upload files.lib.php dol_convert_file code injection

items.summary: Greenbone gvmd before 26.43.0 does not restrict certificate creation. Even the Observer role, documented to be read-only, can execute create_tls_certificate.
items.title: CVE-2026-133494

items.summary: A flaw was found in sssd. A local user can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting the responder service's available file descriptors (system handles used for open connections). By opening and maintaining many concurrent connections to a responder socket while continuing to queue new connection attempts, an attacker can trigger an unthrottled retry loop. This condition leads to high CPU utilization and stalls the service, preventing legitimate identity and authentication requests from being processed.
items.title: Sssd: sssd: denial of service via responder connection retry loop during file descriptor exhaustion

items.summary: A flaw was found in SSSD. When configured to evaluate password expiration warnings before restrictive access rules in LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) environments, an expired-password warning terminates rule evaluation early and treats the access request as successful. A remote authenticated user with an expired password using an alternative authentication method, such as SSH public key authentication, can exploit this flaw to bypass access control restrictions and gain unauthorized access to protected systems.
items.title: Sssd: sssd: access control bypass via premature ldap access rule evaluation

items.summary: A flaw was found in FreeType, specifically within its CID font loader. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by tricking a user into opening content that embeds or references a specially crafted CID-keyed font. This crafted font can cause repeated allocations and decryptions of subroutine data across multiple font dictionaries, leading to excessive memory and CPU consumption. This can result in a denial of service (DoS) for the application or service processing the font, potentially causing it to hang or terminate.
items.title: Freetype: freetype: denial of service via repeated subroutine allocations in cid font loader

items.summary: A flaw was found in SSSD. When configured with the LDAP access provider and `ldap_access_order` including `ppolicy` or `lockout`, a fail-open condition in the LDAP ppolicy access check can occur if a user lookup returns zero results. This can incorrectly return success and cache an allow decision, permitting continued authorization for a deleted or deprovisioned user. A remote attacker with prior valid account context could exploit this to maintain access to information and potentially make limited modifications to resources that should no longer be available.
items.title: Sssd: sssd: fail-open in ldap ppolicy access check allows continued authorization

items.summary:
The code in pppd that formats a response to a PEAP Request packet in peap_response() copies an entire TLS record of up to 16384 bytes into the fixed global buffer outpacket_buf
 without checking the available space and without implementing outgoing 
PEAP fragmentation. Thus a pppd process connecting to a server which 
requests PEAP authentication can be induced to corrupt global static 
data following the outpacket_buf array, most likely causing incorrect behavior or a crash.
items.title: PPPD buffer overflow in PEAP response code

items.summary: A flaw was found in RESTEasy's CorsFilter, which, when configured to allow all origins ("*"), reflects the request's Origin header back in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This permissive cross-origin policy allows a malicious website to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read authenticated responses from a victim's session, resulting in a loss of confidentiality.
items.title: Resteasy-core: resteasy: corsfilter reflects arbitrary origin with credentials under wildcard config

items.summary: A flaw was found in libxml2. A local user or an attacker providing a specially crafted XML catalog can trigger a NULL pointer dereference during XML catalog parsing. This occurs when a `nextCatalog` element lacks its mandatory `catalog` attribute, leading to the application crashing and causing a Denial of Service (DoS).
items.title: Libxml2: libxml2: null pointer dereference parsing nextcatalog without catalog attribute

items.summary: Open Access Management (OpenAM) is an access management solution. From 13.0.0 until 16.1.2, the OAuth2 authorize endpoint's display=wap consent page reflects request-derived values through ConsentRequiredResource and wap/authorize.ftl without HTML escaping. An attacker can induce a user with an active OpenAM session to follow a crafted authorization link and execute JavaScript in the OpenAM origin, enabling session or cookie theft, CSRF-token disclosure, and actions with the victim's privileges. At least one registered OAuth2 client is required, but the attacker does not need to control that client. This issue is fixed in version 16.1.2.
items.title: OpenAM Reflected XSS in the OAuth2/OIDC `wap` consent page

items.summary: A flaw was found in sssd. A local unprivileged user could send a specially crafted request with a zero-length body to the Network Security Services (NSS) responder. This could lead to a denial-of-service condition, causing the NSS responder to become unstable or terminate. This vulnerability affects the availability of the system responder.
items.title: Sssd: sssd: denial of service in nss responder via crafted zero-length requests

items.summary: A flaw was found in SSSD (System Security Services Daemon). A local attacker with privileges to connect to the PAM (Pluggable Authentication Modules) responder socket can send a specially crafted protocol request. If the `pam_app_services` configuration is enabled and the service item is omitted from the request, a NULL pointer dereference can occur. This vulnerability leads to a denial of service, causing the PAM responder to crash and disrupt authentication services.
items.title: Sssd: sssd: local denial of service due to null pointer dereference in pam responder

items.summary: A flaw was found in PCS (Pacemaker Configuration System). A local attacker with membership in the 'haclient' group can exploit the 'pcs host auth --token' command to read the contents of arbitrary files on the filesystem, provided the files are shorter than 256 bytes. The file contents are read with root privileges by the pcsd daemon and can be exfiltrated by the attacker through subsequent cluster node communication. This allows disclosure of sensitive data such as API keys, tokens, or configuration secrets that would otherwise be inaccessible to the attacker.
items.title: Pcs: pcs: non-root haclient users can read arbitrary files via pcs host auth --token

items.summary: A flaw was found in crun. After pivot_root, reopening /dev/null for stdio can follow a symlink and attach a host file to container stdio, then change that file's ownership. Affected versions are crun 1.29.1 and earlier. Default configurations that mount a fresh /dev are not exposed. No fixed release is available yet.
items.title: Crun: crun: /dev/null symlink follow during stdio reopen allows host bind-mount write and chown

items.summary: A flaw was found in crun. When the container configuration does not give /dev a dedicated mount, terminal setup can redirect /dev/console onto an attacker-controlled path, including via the read-only-rootfs bind-mount fallback. Affected versions are crun 1.29.1 and earlier. Default configurations that mount a fresh /dev are not exposed. No fixed release is available yet.
items.title: Crun: crun: /dev/console symlink follow allows root-owned file creation outside the rootfs

items.summary: The cupsUTF32ToUTF8() function in CUPS's cups/transcode.c lacks a source-length bound and can read past the end of the source buffer, resulting in a heap out-of-bounds read. This is reachable via SNMP supply-description parsing in backend/snmp-supplies.c with attacker-controlled content.
items.title: Cups: openprinting cups: heap out-of-bounds read in cupsutf32toutf8() via missing source-length bound

items.summary: A flaw was found in libtpms, a library that provides software TPM 2.0 emulation. When restoring TPM 2.0 state (for example during a virtual machine's power-on or state/migration restore), a malformed state blob can supply an oversized skip-block length that is not validated against the remaining size of the input buffer. This can drive an internal size counter negative, which bypasses a subsequent bounds check due to an unsafe signed-to-unsigned conversion, causing the parser to read memory outside the bounds of the heap buffer holding the state data. Successful exploitation can crash the process hosting libtpms (such as swtpm), resulting in a denial of service of the emulated TPM device and the virtual machine that depends on it. No data corruption or information disclosure was confirmed.
items.title: Libtpms: libtpms: heap out-of-bounds read in tpm2 state unmarshalling via unchecked block_skip_read() blocksize

items.summary: A flaw was found in the MTP backend in gvfs. When reading a file from a mounted MTP device, do_read() in gvfsbackendmtp.c trusts the data length returned by the device without limiting it to the original size requested by the client. If a malicious MTP device responds with more bytes than requested, this unrestricted length is passed directly to memcpy(). This causes the operation to read memory outside the intended boundaries. This allows an attacker who plugs in a malicious MTP device to cause a segmentation fault when a file is read and crash the gvfsd-mtp process, resulting in a denial of service.
items.title: Gvfs: mtp: out-of-bounds read in do_read()

items.summary: A flaw was found in the AFP backend in gvfs. When mounting a share, a malicious AFP server can cause the DSI read path to process a length that exceeds the size requested by the client. The function does not verify the server-provided length against the pre-sized reply buffer, causing the operation to access past the intended boundaries. This issue allows a malicious server to overflow a heap buffer and crash the gvfsd-afp process, resulting in a denial of service.
items.title: Gvfs: afp: heap-based buffer overflow in dsi read path

items.summary: A flaw was found in the SFTP backend in gvfs. When mounting a share, a malicious SFTP server can cause read_string() to allocate a buffer with a certain length but the function does not verify that the buffer is completely filled, leaving the remainder of the buffer containing uninitialized heap contents. If the server sends a short FXP_HANDLE reply, these uninitialized bytes are taken as the file handle. The client will then echo these uninitialized bytes back to the server on all subsequent requests using that handle. With a length of 128 bytes, this issue allows the malicious server to deterministically read uninitialized heap memory from the gvfsd-sftp process, leaking its heap base and the load address of the libgio library, resulting in a deterministic defeat of Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR).
items.title: Gvfs: sftp: uninitialized heap disclosure in read_string()

items.summary:
A flaw was found in gdk-pixbuf. When loading a specially crafted JPEG image containing chunked ICC profile markers, an error during ICC profile parsing can leave stale size metadata after the profile buffer is freed. A subsequent allocation in the same decode can cause an out-of-bounds write, potentially crashing the application. To exploit this flaw, an application using gdk-pixbuf must process the malicious JPEG image.

Affected version >= 2.26.4
items.title: Gdk-pixbuf: gdk-pixbuf: invalid write in jpeg icc profile parser on error recovery

items.summary: A flaw was found in file-roller. When opening or extracting a malicious 7z or RAR archive containing a file entry with an excessively long path, file-roller's progress-line parsing copies the path into a fixed-size stack buffer using an unbounded string copy. This can trigger a stack buffer overflow and cause file-roller to terminate, resulting in a denial of service. To exploit this flaw, a victim must open or extract the crafted archive using file-roller.
items.title: File-roller: file-roller: stack buffer overflow in parse_progress_line for 7z and rar handlers

items.summary:
A flaw was found in CRI-O's container-creation environment-variable handling
(`mergeEnvs` in `server/utils.go`, consumed by `setupContainerEnvironmentAndWorkdir` in
`server/container_create.go`). When a `CreateContainer` request supplies a `nil` CRI
`Envs` field, CRI-O falls back to using the target OCI image's `config.Env` entries
unfiltered, in contrast to the normal merge path, which validates each entry for a
`key=value` form before use. An OCI image whose `config.Env` contains an entry with no
`=` character (e.g. a bare `NOEQUALS` string) causes CRI-O to split that entry into a
single-element slice and then index its second element, which is out of range. This
triggers an unrecovered Go runtime panic in the `crio` daemon process, crashing it and
terminating the container-runtime service for all workloads on the node until it is
restarted.
items.title: Cri-o: cri-o: unvalidated image env var causes daemon crash

items.summary: A flaw was found in FreeIPA. A low-privilege authenticated user can exploit this vulnerability by submitting an oversized One-Time Password (OTP) key value. This oversized key is then decoded and re-encoded without proper size limits, consuming excessive CPU and memory resources. This can lead to a denial of service, degrading the availability of the IPA service.
items.title: Ipa: freeipa: authenticated dos in `otptoken-add` via unbounded otp key decoding/re-encoding

items.summary: A flaw was found in Samba's CTDB, the clustered database service used by Samba. Insufficient integrity validation of received CTDB protocol packets allows malformed packets containing invalid field lengths, improperly terminated strings, or inconsistent packet sizes to be processed without adequate bounds checking. A remote attacker with access to the CTDB private network may trigger a denial of service through process crashes or excessive memory consumption and, in limited cases, disclose adjacent memory contents.
items.title: Samba: ctdb fails to do integrity checking of received packets

items.summary: A flaw was found in iperf3. A remote unauthenticated attacker can exploit a vulnerability in the `JSON_read()` function, which accepts a peer-controlled message length and allocates memory without an upper bound. This allows the attacker to trigger excessive memory consumption, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) through memory exhaustion, severe slowdown, or termination of the iperf3 service.
items.title: Iperf3: unbounded peer-controlled allocation in iperf3 json_read() allows unauthenticated remote memory exhaustion

items.summary: A flaw was found in GIMP. A signed integer overflow vulnerability exists in the `file-fli` plugin when processing FLI image files. This occurs due to an incorrect calculation during memory allocation for image buffers, where the multiplication of image width and height can exceed the maximum integer value. A remote attacker could exploit this by tricking a user into opening a specially crafted FLI file, leading to the application crashing and resulting in a denial of service.
items.title: Gimp: gimp: denial of service via signed integer overflow in fli file processing

items.summary: A stack-based out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in the "s_vlog" function of stunnel, when handling oversized log messages via "vsnprintf". A remote attacker with network access to a stunnel service can send protocol inputs that trigger a log message longer than 1024 bytes, leading to an out-of-bounds stack read and a potential crash. In certain corner cases, the same vulnerability could be used to replace a series of trailing "\n" characters with "\0".
items.title: Stunnel: stack-based out-of-bounds read/write in stunnel s_vlog via oversized log message

items.summary: A Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) bypass vulnerability exists in “stunnel” 5.79 and lower when configured in SOCKS proxy mode. This flaw allows a client to bypass intended localhost restrictions by using IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g., “::ffff:127.0.0.1”) or unspecified addresses ("0.0.0.0", "::"), enabling access to loopback-only services on the "stunnel" host that should not be network-reachable.
items.title: Stunnel: ssrf bypass in stunnel socks proxy via ipv4-mapped ipv6 loopback and unspecified addresses allows access to loopback-only services

items.summary: A flaw was found in the file-icns plugin in GIMP. When applying a decompressed mask during ICNS image processing, the plugin reads from the mask data buffer without verifying if the cursor exceeds the allocated resource size. If a crafted file contains a truncated mask resource, the icns_decompress function continues reading past the bounds of the buffer. This out-of-bounds read vulnerability results in information disclosure of heap contents, where memory contents are leaked as alpha channel pixel values, or a crash leading to a denial of service if unmapped memory is accessed.
items.title: Gimp: out-of-bounds read in file-icns plugin causes information disclosure or crash on crafted icns images

items.summary: A flaw was found in the file-sgi plugin in GIMP. When processing an RLE-compressed SGI image, the plugin allocates memory for a row table. The image header dimensions (ysize and zsize) are read as 16-bit unsigned integers. If a crafted file sets both dimensions to their maximum value (65535), the multiplication ysize * zsize overflows the standard 32-bit int boundary before being passed to calloc. This integer overflow issue results in undefined behavior, aborting the plugin and causing a denial of service.
items.title: Gimp: signed integer overflow in file-sgi (sgi-lib) causes the plugin to crash on rle sgi images

items.summary: A flaw was found in GIMP. The PlayStation TIM loader, responsible for handling PlayStation image files, incorrectly calculates the size of the Color Look-Up Table (CLUT) due to an integer overflow. This occurs when multiplying num_colors and num_cluts, both 16-bit unsigned short integers, resulting in a value exceeding the maximum integer limit. An attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted image file, leading to undefined behavior and causing the GIMP plug-in to abort, effectively resulting in a denial of service.
items.title: Gimp: gimp: denial of service via integer overflow in playstation tim loader

items.summary: A flaw was found in GIMP's PSP file format parser. A double-free condition occurs in the read_layer_block() function when processing a specially crafted PSP file. This could allow an attacker to cause memory corruption, potentially leading to denial of service or arbitrary code execution.
items.title: Gimp: gimp: double-free in read_layer_block()

items.summary: A flaw was found in the libblkid library of util-linux. During nested partition probing, the BSD, Minix, Solaris x86, and UnixWare partition probers cache a raw pointer to a parent partition entry in a dynamically allocated array. When subsequent partition additions cause the array to be reallocated, this pointer becomes stale, leading to a heap use-after-free read. An attacker who can present a crafted block device image (for example, via USB insertion or a loop-mounted disk image) can trigger this flaw without user interaction, as libblkid is invoked automatically by udev/udisks as root on block-device hot-plug events. This could lead to limited information disclosure or denial of service.
items.title: Util-linux: util-linux: heap use-after-free in libblkid nested partition probing

items.summary: A flaw was found in libsolv. This heap buffer overflow vulnerability occurs when a victim processes a specially crafted `.solv` file containing negative size values in the `repo_add_solv` function. This leads to an undersized memory allocation and a subsequent out-of-bounds write. An attacker could exploit this to cause a denial of service (DoS).
items.title: Libsolv: heap buffer overflow in libsolv repo_add_solv via negative maxsize from crafted .solv file

items.summary: A flaw was found in libsolv. This stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability occurs in libsolv's Debian metadata parser when processing specially crafted Debian repository metadata. An attacker could exploit this by providing malicious SHA384 or SHA512 checksum tags, leading to memory corruption and a denial of service (DoS) in the affected system.
items.title: Libsolv: stack-based buffer overflow in libsolv's debian metadata parser when handling sha384/sha512 checksums

items.summary: A flaw was found in libxml2. This vulnerability occurs when the library processes a specially crafted XML Schema Definition (XSD) validated document that includes an internal entity reference. An attacker could exploit this by providing a malicious document, leading to a type confusion error that causes the application to crash. This results in a denial of service (DoS), making the affected system or application unavailable.
items.title: Libxml2: libxml2: denial of service via crafted xsd-validated document

items.summary: A flaw was found in binutils, specifically within the `readelf` utility. This vulnerability allows a local attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by tricking a user into processing a specially crafted Executable and Linkable Format (ELF) file. The exploitation of this flaw can lead to the system becoming unresponsive due to excessive resource consumption or a program crash.
items.title: Binutils: binutils: denial of service via crafted elf file

items.summary: A flaw was found in GIMP. An integer overflow vulnerability exists when processing ICO image files, specifically in the `ico_read_info` and `ico_read_icon` functions. This issue arises because a size calculation for image buffers can wrap around due to a 32-bit integer evaluation, allowing oversized image headers to bypass security checks. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted ICO file, leading to a buffer overflow and memory corruption, which may result in an application level denial of service.
items.title: Gimp: gimp: memory corruption due to integer overflow in ico file handling

items.summary: A flaw was found in GIMP's PSP (Paint Shop Pro) file parser. A remote attacker could exploit an integer overflow vulnerability in the read_creator_block() function by providing a specially crafted PSP image file. This vulnerability occurs when a 32-bit length value from the file is used for memory allocation without proper validation, leading to a heap overflow and an out-of-bounds write. Successful exploitation could result in an application level denial of service.
items.title: Gimp: gimp: denial of service via crafted psp image file

items.summary: A flaw was found in Keycloak. An administrator with `manage-clients` permission can exploit a misconfiguration where this permission is equivalent to `manage-permissions`. This allows the administrator to escalate privileges and gain control over roles, users, or other administrative functions within the realm. This privilege escalation can occur when admin permissions are enabled at the realm level.
items.title: Keycloak: org.keycloak/keycloak-services: keycloak: privilege escalation via manage-clients permission

items.summary: A flaw was found in Keycloak. The User-Managed Access (UMA) 2.0 Protection API endpoint for permission tickets fails to enforce the `uma_protection` role check. This allows any authenticated user with a token issued for a resource server client, even without the `uma_protection` role, to enumerate all permission tickets in the system. This vulnerability partial leads to information disclosure.
items.title: Keycloak: keycloak: information disclosure via improper role enforcement in uma 2.0 protection api

items.summary: A flaw was found in libsoup. An integer underflow vulnerability occurs when processing content with a zero-length resource, leading to a buffer overread. This can allow an attacker to potentially access sensitive information or cause an application level denial of service.
items.title: Libsoup: libsoup: buffer overread due to integer underflow when handling zero-length resources

items.summary: A flaw was found in Keycloak. An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger an application level Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a highly compressed SAMLRequest through the SAML Redirect Binding. The server fails to enforce size limits during DEFLATE decompression, leading to an OutOfMemoryError (OOM) and subsequent process termination. This vulnerability allows an attacker to disrupt the availability of the service.
items.title: Keycloak: keycloak: denial of service due to excessive samlrequest decompression

items.summary: A flaw was found in libsoup. An attacker controlling the value used to set the Content-Type header can inject a Carriage Return Line Feed (CRLF) sequence due to improper input sanitization in the `soup_message_headers_set_content_type()` function. This vulnerability allows for the injection of arbitrary header-value pairs, potentially leading to HTTP header injection and response splitting attacks.
items.title: Libsoup: libsoup: http header injection and response splitting via crlf injection in content-type header

items.summary: A flaw was found in GNU Binutils. This heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability, specifically an out-of-bounds read in the bfd linker, allows an attacker to gain access to sensitive information. By convincing a user to process a specially crafted XCOFF object file, an attacker can trigger this flaw, potentially leading to information disclosure or an application level denial of service.
items.title: Binutils: gnu binutils: information disclosure via specially crafted xcoff object file

items.summary: A flaw was found in GNU Binutils. This vulnerability, a heap-based buffer overflow, specifically an out-of-bounds read, exists in the bfd linker component. An attacker could exploit this by convincing a user to process a specially crafted malicious XCOFF object file. Successful exploitation may lead to the disclosure of sensitive information or cause the application to crash, resulting in an application level denial of service.
items.title: Binutils: gnu binutils: information disclosure or denial of service via out-of-bounds read in bfd linker

items.summary: A flaw was found in Libsoup. The server-side digest authentication implementation in the SoupAuthDomainDigest class does not properly track issued nonces or enforce the required incrementing nonce-count (nc) attribute. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to capture a single valid authentication header and replay it repeatedly. Consequently, the attacker can bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to protected resources, impersonating the legitimate user.
items.title: Libsoup: libsoup: authentication bypass via digest authentication replay attack

items.summary: A flaw was found in Keycloak. An administrator with `manage-users` permission can bypass the "Only administrators can view" setting for unmanaged attributes, allowing them to modify these attributes. This improper access control can lead to unauthorized changes to user profiles, even when the system is configured to restrict such modifications.
items.title: Org.keycloak/keycloak-services: keycloak: unauthorized modification of unmanaged user attributes by administrators

items.summary: A flaw was found in the github.com/containers/image library. This flaw allows attackers to trigger unexpected authenticated registry accesses on behalf of a victim user, causing resource exhaustion, local path traversal, and other attacks.
items.title: Containers/image: digest type does not guarantee valid type
